title: Protect the sleep period
text: NASA's standard schedules an 8.5-hour sleep period and keeps critical tasks out of the 1 to 7 AM body-clock low. NASA sleep guidance lists sleep hygiene, light, naps and, only after other options, medication. ISS crews average about 6.1 hours of sleep per night.

title: Use the lighting schedule
text: The ISS lighting system has three settings: general (4500 K), pre-sleep (2700 K, warm) and phase-shift (6500 K, bright blue-white) to help move the body clock.

title: Re-test and rest before critical work
text: The Reaction Self-Test was flown so crews could check their own alertness. In ISS data, nights under 6 hours were linked to slower responses.

title: Return to the exercise prescription
text: ISS crews are scheduled 2.5 hours a day, six days a week, on resistive and aerobic devices. Resistive exercise with good nutrition kept hip and pelvis bone density at pre-flight levels on 4 to 6 month flights. NASA's standard is to keep aerobic capacity and strength at or above 80% of baseline.

title: Drink toward the fluid target
text: In-flight prescriptions are 2.0 to 2.5 litres a day; modelling suggests more lowers kidney-stone risk further. Low urine volume is the main modifiable stone risk in space.

title: Eat the planned menu
text: NASA's standard is to provide 100% of calculated energy needs, yet crews have eaten about 80% and lost 3 to 4% of body mass, mostly in the first month.

title: Check air revitalization and move to better airflow
text: ISS operations lowered the cabin limit from 4.0 to 3.0 mmHg (24-hour average) after crews reported headaches and missed procedure steps. Each extra 1 mmHg doubled the odds of a headache report. Carbon dioxide can pool in poorly ventilated spots. Moving and raising local ventilation is our inference from that finding, not a quoted procedure.

title: Solar storm: shelter
text: The Orion plan is to build a shelter from stowage bags within an hour and stay up to 24 hours. Spacewalks are ended or delayed and the crew moves to the most shielded area. Career limit: under 600 mSv.

title: Symptom check, rest, limit spread, consult
text: On Earth, wearables showed resting heart rate rising a median of 7 bpm about 4 days before infection symptoms. Immune function changes in space and latent viruses reactivate in most ISS crew. NASA lists hygiene, quarantine and monitoring as countermeasures.

title: Private medical conference
text: NASA's medical operations standard gives every crew member private medical conferences: real time when possible, store-and-forward when communication is delayed.

title: Private psychological conference and family contact
text: The same standard provides private psychological conferences. NASA also names family contact, journaling and meaningful activities as behavioral health countermeasures.

title: Expect space motion sickness early
text: 60 to 80% of space travellers have motion sickness in the first 2 to 3 days of weightlessness, and a similar share after returning to gravity.

title: Repeat the oxygen reading at rest
text: Clinical guidance on Earth: normal is 95 to 100%; contact a clinician at 92% or below; 88% or below is urgent. In-flight norms were not verified.

title: Vision self-check and report
text: About 70% of long-duration crew show early signs of spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome. There is no proven countermeasure yet, so changes should be recorded and reported.

title: Medical clearance before a spacewalk
text: NASA's standard requires medical clearance before every spacewalk.
